title: Projectile Motion
subcategory: Motion in a Plane — Projectile Motion

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Motion in a Plane

summary: A projectile undergoes independent, simultaneous horizontal (constant velocity) and vertical (constant acceleration g) motion, tracing a parabolic path.
explanation: The key idea (Galileo's insight) is that horizontal and vertical motions of a projectile are completely independent of each other and can be analysed separately, then combined. For a projectile launched with speed u at angle θ above the horizontal: horizontal velocity ux = u cosθ stays constant throughout (no horizontal force, ignoring air resistance), while vertical velocity uy = u sinθ changes under gravity (a = −g). This gives three standard results: time of flight T = 2u sinθ/g, maximum height H = u²sin²θ/2g, and horizontal range R = u²sin2θ/g. Range is maximum at θ = 45°, and R is the same for complementary angles (e.g. 30° and 60°) since sin2θ has the same value for θ and (90°−θ). The path traced is a parabola: y = x tanθ − gx²/(2u²cos²θ). Air resistance, which real projectiles experience, is neglected in this NCERT-level treatment, so it strictly applies to motion in vacuum near Earth's surface.
commonMisconceptions: Believing the horizontal velocity decreases as the projectile rises — it stays constant throughout the flight since gravity has no horizontal component.
Forgetting that maximum range at 45° assumes launch and landing at the same height; if launched from a height, the optimal angle is less than 45°.
Mixing up which trig function goes with which component — horizontal uses cosθ, vertical uses sinθ, a very common exam slip.
examples: A ball kicked at 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal lands back at the same height it was kicked from, after tracing a parabolic arc.
A bullet fired horizontally from a height and a bullet simply dropped from the same height hit the ground at the same time — vertical motion is identical in both cases.
genZNote: Horizontal motion said 'not my problem' — gravity only handles the vertical drama.
